title: Replicating honesty steering on a long-horizon agentic task (does it survive multi-turn?)

original_idea.body:
# Replicating honesty steering on a long-horizon agentic task (does it survive multi-turn?)

**Problem:** Honesty/deception steering is almost always evaluated on single-turn QA. Whether a honesty steering vector still works over a multi-turn agentic interaction (where a model might pursue a hidden goal) is an unexplored replication regime.

**Direction:** Set up a simple multi-turn text scenario (e.g., a public 'insider-trading' style deception eval) on a small open model, apply an honesty steering vector throughout, and measure whether deception is reduced across turns vs. single-turn. Twist: replicate honesty steering in a multi-turn, goal-directed setting.

**Why it matters:** A model that pursues a secret long-horizon goal while appearing honest turn-by-turn is a core scheming threat model. Testing whether cheap steering interventions hold up across turns is a feasible model-organism-flavored slice that no lab is uniquely positioned to run.

**Relevant context:** Linear deception probes generalize to insider-trading scenarios; Apollo-style deception evals; RepE honesty steering.
